lesson.title: Hallo, Dag & Alsjeblieft
lesson.subtitle: greetings, thanks and the politeness set

hook.title: The First Words You Actually Say
hook.content: Hallo, dag, dank je, alsjeblieft: the first Dutch words are mostly twins or loans. The set is small, and each word has a clear social job.

pattern.title: Greet, thank, ask
pattern.content: Hallo and goedemorgen greet; dag can greet or say goodbye; dank je thanks; alsjeblieft and graag handle please. The forms are fixed, so learn them as whole social moves.
pattern.trap_note: Dag is not only 'day'; as a greeting it means 'bye'. Context and tone decide.

exercises.prompt: Match each English meaning with its Dutch twin (Hallo, Dag & Alsjeblieft):
exercises.target_answer: hallo, de dag, dank, alsjeblieft, goedemorgen, graag
exercises.meaning: hello, day; bye, thanks, please, good morning, gladly; please
exercises.explanation: These are the anchors of "Hallo, Dag & Alsjeblieft": read each Dutch form through the pattern, not as a new word.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence says: “Hello, how are you?”?
exercises.explanation: “Hallo, hoe gaat het?” is the Dutch form; the other readings bend the pattern of “Hallo, Dag & Alsjeblieft”.
“Goedemorgen.” puts the thought together the Dutch way — Greet, thank, ask.

diagnosis.slip: an English-shaped word order slipped in
diagnosis.cue: Dag is not only 'day'; as a greeting it means 'bye'. Context and tone decide.

exercises.prompt: Which English sentence is built the Dutch way?
exercises.explanation: “Dank je wel.” is word-for-word “Thank you well.”. The odd English is the lesson — never a model to produce. Pattern: Greet, thank, ask.

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
exercises.explanation: “Alsjeblieft.” reuses only material taught in “Hallo, Dag & Alsjeblieft” — Greet, thank, ask.
exercises.affirmation: You heard “Alsjeblieft.” — a sentence built from the lesson's own Dutch, practising Greet, thank, ask.

twist.prompt: One more, no safety net — say: “See you tomorrow!”
twist.explanation: Tot ('until') + morgen ('tomorrow') is the standard goodbye.

summary.outcome: Greet, thank, ask politely and say goodbye with the core Dutch set.
summary.takeaway: Politeness is a small closed set; learn the moves, not just the words.
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next on De Brug: Vowels & Diphthongs.

hallo.etymology_derivation: A 19th-century loan from English; Dutch welcomed it whole.

dag.etymology_derivation: English day is the same word; Dutch also uses dag as a goodbye.

dank.etymology_derivation: English thank is the same root; Dutch d is the hardened th.

alsjeblieft.etymology_derivation: A whole polite sentence worn down into one word.

goedemorgen.etymology_derivation: goed + morgen: the same compound as English good morning.

graag.etymology_derivation: The adverb of willingness; Dutch uses it where English says 'like to'.
